static_traits.name: Zhang Jing
static_traits.medical_history: Self-reports having Asperger syndrome; has not received treatment for similar psychological problems; no significant other medical history
static_traits.language_features: Tends to understand things literally; clear and coherent expression, high cooperation; able to self-reflect and propose feasible strategies; prone to anxiety and self-doubt after small setbacks; positive and polite attitude

basic_info.main_problem: I tend to take everything literally and often dismiss the positive. I recently started a new job, and stepping on chewed gum on my way to work - a small thing - significantly affected my confidence.
basic_info.core_demands: Stepping on chewing gum this time made me realize that my tendency to disqualify the positive has affected my confidence, so I decided to seek counseling to address this problem.
growth_experiences: Long-standing Asperger traits (tendency toward literal understanding, relatively difficult social learning); has not received psychotherapy or counseling before; the current social support system is weak, and the client lacks people to discuss problems with when they arise.

special_situations.event: Stepping on chewed gum on the way to work
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If even such a small thing happens to me, it means I will fail and cannot handle the new job
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Becomes overly cautious at work with repeated self-doubt, trying to avoid further mistakes by strengthening control
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: This shows I am not good enough; I will not succeed in the new job

special_situations.event: Any small mistake or unexpected situation occurring in the new job
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: As long as there is a little problem, it proves I am not good enough and do not have competence
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Focuses only on the negative and ignores positive evidence and successful experiences

special_situations.event: Successfully completes several projects and has friendly interactions with colleagues
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: Good performance is just chance; it does not prove I am truly capable
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Negates or devalues positive experiences; does not record or reinforce them
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: This time was just luck; it does not mean I am capable

special_situations.event: A short time after experiencing positive progress
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: Good things will not last; problems will arise sooner or later
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Anticipating negative outcomes in advance and staying highly vigilant to avoid disappointment
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: Something will go wrong again soon; I cannot hold up

core_conflict.wish: Longing to be affirmed and accepted, being seen as a capable person in the new job
core_conflict.fear: Fearing failure and being negated, worrying small setbacks will expose one's incompetence
defense_goal: Reducing the risk of disappointment and criticism by negating the positive and being overly cautious
Maintaining vigilance toward the outside world to preserve a sense of psychological safety

object_relations.self_representation: A novice who is not good enough, prone to mistakes
object_relations.object_representation: The outside world / environment is like a harsh judge (even treating random events as 'the universe negating me')

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When encountering small setbacks (such as stepping on chewing gum) or small mistakes at work
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Regards incidental events as the outside world negating them (such as 'the universe is telling me I cannot'), and infers low self-worth from this
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Uses a definite and pessimistic tone, interpreting occasional events as others' negation; uses absolute words (such as 'all' and 'definitely'), ignores or downplays positive evidence, and avoids discussing factual details and alternative explanations.

manifestations: Currently lacking a strong social support system to discuss troubles with
In the new job, 'socialization' is a new learning challenge, feeling helpless
Positive experiences 'cannot be kept' and are often erased by negative events
Completing projects and friendly interactions are hard to convert into a stable sense of worth and self-affirmation
outcomes: Holding pessimistic expectations about the future, with intensified mood swings

contact_model.definition: The individual attributes feelings they find hard to accept in themselves to others or the outside world, regarding inner experience as the outside world's evaluation of them.
manifestations: Interpreting stepping on chewing gum as the outside world / 'the universe' negating oneself
Treats occasional negative events as conclusive judgments by others or the environment about own ability

contact_model.definition: The individual has poor self-reflection and excessive self-restriction and self-blame, and is overly cautious about contact.
manifestations: Excessive caution at work, repeated self-doubt
Difficulty concentrating and decreased efficiency due to worry about making mistakes

exception_events.target_problem: When encountering small setbacks in a new work environment, the client usually becomes excessively anxious, disqualifies the positive, and has damaged confidence in social settings, with work performance becoming overly cautious and hesitant.
exception_events.unique_outcome: In several work tasks after starting the job, the client successfully completed several projects and felt happy and relieved in the moment; interactions with colleagues were friendly, and confidence in these moments was higher than usual.
exception_events.reason: Different support: colleagues were friendly and interactions went smoothly; different context: completing the task brought concrete results and a sense of achievement; different understanding: at that moment the client saw evidence of their own competence, and the positive experience became apparent.

positive_force: Willing to seek help and having self-reflection ability
Objective evidence of successfully completed projects already exists for reinforcement
Friendly colleagues, a potential interpersonal support resource
Positive attitude; willing to try recording positive events (such as journaling)
negative_force: Cognitive biases such as disqualifying the positive, mental filtering, black-and-white thinking are significant
Lacks a strong social support system; insufficient emotion-regulation resources
Asperger traits lead to a tendency toward literal interpretation and social difficulties
After small setbacks, tends toward catastrophic expectations and self-labeling

target_behavior.behavior: After encountering small setbacks, shows at work excessive caution, repeated self-doubt and reduced attention, and insufficient confidence in social settings
antecedent: Minor unexpected incidents such as stepping on chewing gum on the way to work
Uncertainty of a new work environment and learning pressure
Minor mistakes or disruptions occur at work
target_behavior.core_reason: All-or-nothing thinking, mental filtering, and disqualifying-the-positive cognitive interpretations driven by negative core beliefs ('I am not good enough', 'I will not succeed'); Asperger traits make the client more inclined to literal understanding and find it difficult to flexibly restate the meaning of events.
target_behavior.function: Through excessive caution and self-monitoring, escapes failure risks and external criticism, trying to obtain a sense of control and psychological safety.
target_behavior.consequence: Work efficiency and focus declined, social confidence damaged, anxiety intensified, and positive experiences are hard to internalize into stable self-affirmation.
